transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-12
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jules Navarro (CSM), Lisa Monroe (BlueElm Dir Product), Rajesh Iyer (BlueElm CTO), Maria Gomez (BlueElm InfoSec), Tomás Ruiz (BlueElm ML Eng), Ellen Park (BlueElm Procurement)

Summary:
Quick sync to close out the 4-week pilot: review metrics, confirm success criteria met or gaps, align stakeholders on business case and next steps for production. Discussed latency/cost tradeoffs, security signoffs, and SOW timelines. Agreed on deliverables: final results spreadsheet, config recommendations, and contract review.

Topics:
- Pilot results review (accuracy, latency, cost)
- Tuning and configuration recommendations (batching, quant, KV cache)
- Security/Legal checkpoints (SOC 2, KMS, data retention)
- Production roll plan and timeline
- Commercial next steps (SOW, PO)

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll give folks a couple seconds, and then Samir and I will walk through the final pilot numbers and next steps. Quick agenda in the deck we shared — final results, tuning recs, and the business case closeout.

[00:00:22] Lisa Monroe: Sounds good. Appreciate you setting this up. We've got five people on from product and infra plus procurement joining shortly.

[00:00:31] Rajesh Iyer: Hi—sorry I'm a little late, hopping in now.

[00:00:36] Avery Chen: No worries Rajesh. Quick roll call — Samir, you set the baseline numbers?

[00:00:42] Samir Patel: Yep, I have them. I'll share screen in a sec — pardon the typos in the spreadsheet, it's a working artifact. So baseline: over the 2-week heavy run we saw the Redwood hosted endpoint sustain 65 RPS for the 2048-token average request patterns, with p50 latency at 118ms and p95 at 410ms on the documented model variant. Cost landed at roughly $1.8 per 1k requests, which normalizes to about $0.025 per average interaction in your flows.

[00:01:18] Tomás Ruiz: Quick question, when you say 2048 token average that's tokenized? Our messages are usually shorter — around 400 tokens average — so curious which number matters for us.

[00:01:29] Samir Patel: Good catch, Tomás. We ran mixed traffic: the heavy experiments purposely used a 2k tail to stress test long contexts (clinical notes). For the read/write front door typical P50s for a 400-token median were ~82ms. I should add that to the sheet to avoid confusion — will annotate.

[00:01:54] Lisa Monroe: OK, that's helpful. So on our actual app distribution the latency numbers look even better.

[00:02:02] Avery Chen: Right — and the key metric the business is asking about is cost per resolved case and end-to-end latency for user workflow. We mapped that to success criteria: p50 < 120ms on median flows, average cost per case <$0.45, and precision@5 for the rerank > 0.88.

[00:02:22] Maria Gomez: On security, we still need to confirm retention windows and whether any raw transcripts are stored in third-party logs. The pilot noted a short-term debug log capture — we need clear removal dates.

[00:02:33] Samir Patel: Yes, we set debug logging off by default; the hosted flow for the pilot had log retention 7 days. For production we recommend 0 days for PII flows and proxy logs to your KMS for audit only. We'll document the recommended KMS/HSM flow.

[00:02:53] Rajesh Iyer: Also want to call out network egress and region placement — we saw modest variance when routing to us-east vs us-west. For data residency we need VPC options.

[00:03:05] Avery Chen: Totally. We covered Redwood Private as an option — VPC peering, customer-managed subnets — and that was one of the paths if you need to bring it on-prem later.

[00:03:20] Tomás Ruiz: Did you test the quantized variant? We have limited GPU footprint locally, so 8-bit quantization would be great if quality holds.

[00:03:29] Samir Patel: Yes — we ran a 4-bit quant test on a dev node. Quality drop was within 1.5% absolute on our rerank metric; latency improved ~28% and cost per token dropped ~43%. Quality regressions are visible in edge cases — we flagged a few hallucination tops in long clinical narratives — I'll share the eval set.

[00:03:50] Lisa Monroe: When you say hallucination tops, can you show an example?

[00:03:55] Samir Patel: Sure — slide 7 has three examples. They are borderline cases where rare entity linking failed. It's fixable by prompt anchoring and a small post-rerank filter.

[00:04:05] Maria Gomez: We need to ensure PHI never leaves the VPC in the final design. Pilot relaxed some of that to measure speed. If going to hosted, we need encryption-at-rest and KMS integration plus a SOC-2 attestation.

[00:04:16] Avery Chen: Understood. Redwood's SOC-2 report and security packet were shared in the drive — link in chat — but for PHI use we typically recommend out-of-band private deployment.

[00:04:26] Ellen Park: From procurement, timeline question — if we greenlight, what's the earliest prod date? We need costs for our FY quarter planning.

[00:04:33] Samir Patel: Earliest realistic is 6-8 weeks for hosted with SSO and audit logging turned on; for VPC/private it's 10-14 weeks given network and security reviews. Exact timing depends on SOW sign-off and infra handoffs.

[00:04:48] Rajesh Iyer: And can you support a phased rollout? Start hosted with redacted data, then move to private once SOC/legal signoff occurs?

[00:04:55] Avery Chen: Yes, that's the recommended pattern — start hosted to hit product milestones then migrate traffic to Redwood Dedicated or Private when compliance checks are closed.

[00:05:08] Lisa Monroe: Let's walk through the business case numbers. Avery, you had a slide mapping pilot gains to savings?

[00:05:14] Avery Chen: Yep. Slide 10 — we projected a 22% reduction in agent handling time because of automation, translating to $320k annualized savings for your current load. With the cost per case at $0.38 under the pilot config and projected throughput, the ROI hits a payback in under nine months assuming 30% adoption.

[00:05:34] Tomás Ruiz: Those are modelled numbers — what are the sensitivities? Like if adoption is only 15%?

[00:05:40] Avery Chen: Good point — slide 11 shows sensitivity. At 15% adoption payback moves to ~18 months; the threshold for positive NPV in year one is ~22% adoption. I'll attach the sensitivity spreadsheet.

[00:05:56] Maria Gomez: Regarding compliance, will you store any audit logs outside our account? We require audit chain control.

[00:06:03] Samir Patel: No, for Dedicated and Private models logs can be forwarded to your SIEM and retained per your retention policy. Hosted will keep some operational logs but can be configured to forward or not store request payloads. There was a slight mistrans in the pilot notes — "K V cash" shows up in a few transcripts — that was meant to be KV cache.

[00:06:21] Lisa Monroe: Ha, yes I saw 'K V cash' — thought we had a finance question for a second.

[00:06:25] Avery Chen: OK, jumping to success criteria — as we discussed earlier, you had three primary gates: latency under 120ms p50, cost per case under $0.45, and model precision@5 > 0.88. Based on current runs: p50 median = 82ms (on real traffic), cost = $0.38, precision@5 = 0.892. So we are within the thresholds.

[00:06:51] Rajesh Iyer: Those numbers look good. Any caveats for production?

[00:06:55] Samir Patel: A couple: long context tail cases still push p95 up — you may want a fallback shorter context path; also quantization aggressive settings can impact rare-entity scores. We recommend a mixed fleet: quant for bulk low-latency calls, full-precision for sensitive long-context ops.

[00:07:14] Tomás Ruiz: How does the mixed fleet routing work? Is it automatic?

[00:07:18] Samir Patel: Redwood supports policy-based smart routing — route by request type, latency SLO, or cost center. We can show the routing rules we've used in the pilot.

[00:07:28] Lisa Monroe: From product side, we need guardrails around which user journeys go to which model. We'll define regions and triggers.

[00:07:35] Avery Chen: Great — action: Samir to export routing rule examples and a recommended default config.

[00:07:42] Samir Patel: Noted.

[00:07:45] Ellen Park: On contracting, what does the commercial look like? Term and commitments?

[00:07:50] Avery Chen: For Dedicated/Private we'll propose a reserved capacity commitment with a 12-month term typically, with credits for ramping and a pilot conversion clause. For hosted there's a usage tier discount schedule in the SOW. I'll attach a redlineable SOW.

[00:08:04] Ellen Park: Can you send a sample SOW and T&Cs?

[00:08:07] Avery Chen: Yep, will send immediately after this call.

[00:08:11] Maria Gomez: Also on encryption — we need to validate KMS flow and key rotation cadence. Can you provide the integration spec?

[00:08:18] Samir Patel: We'll include the KMS/HSM integration spec and rotation cadence in the security packet.

[00:08:23] Rajesh Iyer: One more infra question: autoscaling and cold-starts. In the pilot we saw a couple of cold start spikes when traffic ramped fast. Is there a warm pool pattern?

[00:08:32] Samir Patel: Yes, Redwood can maintain warm pools and tensioned prewarmed instances for burst profiles. In Dedicated we can configure a baseline pool to eliminate cold starts.

[00:08:42] Lisa Monroe: That would be necessary for our peak windows.

[00:08:45] Avery Chen: OK, closing thoughts — we've validated success criteria, identified a few production caveats (long tail p95, PHI retention, contract timing). Proposed next steps are the three items in the chat: final results + cost model, SOW, and infra deep dive.

[00:09:02] Tomás Ruiz: Sounds good. Any blockers on our side?

[00:09:06] Maria Gomez: I need the explicit examples of any data that might be logged and the remediation plan. Once I have that I can sign off on the high-level security posture and route a ticket to legal for consent.

[00:09:18] Samir Patel: We'll include a redacted log sample and the deletion policy in the package.

[00:09:23] Ellen Park: Procurement will need a cost estimate with payment terms to start PO discussion — please ensure it's granular (monthly, usage, reserved).

[00:09:33] Avery Chen: We'll do that.

[00:09:36] Lisa Monroe: On stakeholders, who needs to be in the SOW review? I'll include product leads and Rajesh's infra team. Ellen will loop legal.

[00:09:44] Ellen Park: Yes I'll loop legal and finance.

[00:09:47] Avery Chen: Cool. Quick timeline check: Avery (me) to send final pilot spreadsheet + cost model by 2025-03-19. Samir to send tunings/quant playbook by 2025-03-18. Maria to confirm data examples and retention by 2025-03-20. Ellen to return SOW comments by 2025-03-26. We aligned on a production readiness deep-dive in the week of 2025-03-24 — Samir and Tomás to schedule.

[00:10:12] Rajesh Iyer: OK, I just want to confirm the fallback model policy — if production sees >5% degradation in quality we'll automatically rollback to the full-precision variant. Is that supported?

[00:10:24] Samir Patel: Yes, we can configure automatic rollback on quality regressions tied to eval harness checks or manual threshold. We'll add that to the runbook.

[00:10:33] Lisa Monroe: Good. Anything else?

[00:10:36] Tomás Ruiz: Quick note — we need a one-page exec summary for the steering committee — can you include savings and timeline?

[00:10:42] Avery Chen: We'll produce an exec one-pager with topline ROI, SLOs achieved, and risks.

[00:10:47] Ellen Park: That will help legal/procurement move faster.

[00:10:50] Avery Chen: Great. We'll wrap. Thanks everyone for the time — we'll follow up with the artifacts.

[00:10:57] Lisa Monroe: Thanks all.

[00:11:00] (Call ends, brief side discussion off-record)

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-hears ("K V cache" written as "K V cash"), speaker overlap at 00:06:20, some punctuation omissions typical of autodirect transcripts.
